Its three sources are repository-level, not per instance: the member readers are code in `scripts/downstream-runs.ts`, the publish verifiers are `publish-verify`'s set, and run records live under the auditor's own `qa` directory. Asked per instance it would judge the platform's members against an instance's Tools and report every one as undeclared.

not evaluated: `actor-roles-resolve` is `repo`-scoped and this run is scoped to smart-base. An actor is declared ONCE for the whole repository (`cat-harness/scenarios/actors/`) while a role is a swimlane inside one instance's diagrams, so this compares a repository-level set against an instance-level one. MEASURED 2026-09-26: `--instance ./bootstrap` produced 73 findings, one for almost every one of the 36 repository actors, because they name roles the bootstrap graph does not declare. Every one was false.

Re-asking per instance would re-derive the root's own answer once per declaration and report the same findings N times.
